## Natural history notes

A small colorful ground beetle characterized by a shiny green to bluish-green body, slender legs, and a fast-moving, flattened form typical of foliage-associated carabids. In Florida, Lebia viridis is part of the state’s ground beetle fauna and is most often associated with forest edges, open fields, shrubs, and other vegetated habitats where small insect prey are available. Adults are predatory on small insects, while some Lebia larvae are known to develop as parasitoids of leaf beetle larvae or pupae, making this beetle part of the natural enemy community in plant-rich habitats.
